title: Terraform module: hardware key provider + secrets sync for Private Deployments
creator: Maya Chen
description: Create a reusable Terraform module to enable hardware-backed key providers (cloud KMS or on-prem HSM) and two-way secrets synchronization between the tenant's secrets store (HashiCorp Vault running in VPC) and cloud Secrets Manager (optional). The module must be suitable for Redwood Private deployments running in customer VPCs: it will provision IAM roles/policies, VPC endpoints, KMS key bindings, HSM connectors where applicable, Vault bootstrap resources (auth methods, transit mount subscription), a secrets sync controller (Terraform deploys the Kubernetes custom resources and service account), and health-checking Lambda/sidecar probes that exercise key wrapping/unwrapping and secret retrieval. Module goals: secure key usage with least privilege, deterministic upgrade path for existing customers, clear observability and alerting hooks, and support for automated rotation workflows. This ticket covers design, Terraform implementation, test harnesses (terratest + integration), and rollout plan including migration steps for customers on legacy modules.
acceptance_criteria: Module exposes variables for cloud KMS key id OR HSM connector endpoint and credentials
Module provisions VPC interface endpoints and private DNS for Vault/Secrets Manager where required
Module creates IAM roles/policies scoped to the minimal actions required for wrapping/unwrapping and secret read/write
Built-in health-check resources that run synthetic wrap/unwrap and secret read to a dedicated monitoring metric
Automated migration path documented: two-phase rollout (read-only sync -> write cutover) and terraform plan/apply examples
Integration tests (terratest) validate: KMS crypto operations, Vault transit key usage, secrets sync controller CRUD, and failure recovery
Module tested across AWS and an HSM simulator (softHSM) for CI reproducibility
Security review checklist completed and SRE runbook with alert thresholds published
implementation_notes: Prefer separate submodules: providers/, iam/, vault-bootstrap/, sync-controller/, healthchecks/ to keep plan/apply focused
Use provider aliasing so a single root module can support both customer-managed Vault and Redwood-managed cloud Secrets Manager
Expose 'migration_mode' variable with values: 'legacy', 'read-only-sync', 'cutover' to support stepwise upgrades
Healthchecks implement exponential backoff and circuit-breaker: failures increment a custom CloudWatch metric 'SecretsSync.HealthCheck.Failures'
Rotation flow: leverage Vault transit keys for application-level unwrapping, KMS for DEK encryption of stored payloads; document key rotation playbook
Terraform state: recommend remote state per-customer with state locking; module outputs (key ids, role ARNs) must be marked sensitive
Integration test harness will inject short-lived test keys and secrets, then destroy to avoid long-lived secrets in CI

risk_mitigation: Failure mode: KMS permission misconfiguration -> mitigation: fail-fast healthcheck and explicit preflight terraform apply that validates IAM assumptions
Failure mode: Drift between Vault and Secrets Manager -> mitigation: detect via periodic reconciliation job and alert on >1% divergence
Failure mode: Secret rotation causing app outages -> mitigation: staggered rotation with canary workloads and short TTL test secrets
Failure mode: HSM vendor API flakiness -> mitigation: circuit-breaker with automatic retry and fallback to cached DEK for read-only reads
migration_plan: Phase 0 - Audit: run terraform plan with audit-mode to collect existing keys/roles and secrets references
Phase 1 - Read-only sync: enable sync controller to copy secrets Vault->Secrets Manager without writing back
Phase 2 - Validation: run golden traffic against canary services pointed at synced secrets; measure latency/latency impact
Phase 3 - Cutover: enable writeback and rotate application credentials (short TTL). Monitor health metrics for 24h before full rollout
Rollback: revert migration_mode to 'read-only-sync' and restore previous key bindings; documented in runbook
qa_plan: Unit: terraform validate + fmt + tflint in CI
Integration: terratest scenario using AWS sandbox account + softHSM; validate wrap/unwrap and sync correctness
E2E: deploy module in private-deploy-staging VPC and run synthetic traffic for 12h with induced failures (IAM deny, HSM timeout)
Performance: measure latency added by KMS/HSM calls and ensure 95th percentile < 120ms for key unwrap in typical request patterns
